quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a contrast, and you don't add 'but' in the same sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: Although it was raining, we decided to walk to the restaurant.
quests.correctAnswer: Although it was raining, we decided to walk to the restaurant.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Although' /ɔːlˈðəʊ/ is stressed on THOH and has a voiced /ð/. 'Decided' /dɪˈsaɪdɪd/ is stressed on SIDE.

quests.explanation: 'Even though' is a stronger form of 'although' and is very common in conversation.
quests.textToSpeak: I enjoyed the course, even though the teacher spoke quite quickly.
quests.correctAnswer: I enjoyed the course, even though the teacher spoke quite quickly.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Though' /ðəʊ/ has a voiced /ð/. 'Quickly' /ˈkwɪkli/ starts with /kw/. 'Spoke' /spəʊk/ starts with /sp/.

quests.hint: Hold 'politely' as one stress group: po-LITE-ly.
quests.explanation: 'Keep + -ing' shows she continued, and 'although' reveals what was really happening.
quests.textToSpeak: She kept smiling politely, although she clearly wanted to leave.
quests.correctAnswer: She kept smiling politely, although she clearly wanted to leave.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Politely' /pəˈlaɪtli/ is stressed on LITE. 'Clearly' /ˈklɪəli/ starts with /kl/. 'Wanted to' can sound like 'wanna'.

quests.explanation: After 'when', use the present tense ('get') even for a future meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: When I get to the station, I'll text you so we can meet up.
quests.correctAnswer: When I get to the station, I'll text you so we can meet up.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Text you' /tekst ju/ merges into a /tʃ/-like sound. 'Meet up' links: mee-tup. 'Station' /ˈsteɪʃn/.

quests.explanation: 'Have to' expresses a requirement, and 'when' sets up the situation.
quests.textToSpeak: I always feel nervous when I have to speak in front of people.
quests.correctAnswer: I always feel nervous when I have to speak in front of people.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Nervous' /ˈnɜːvəs/ is stressed on NER. 'Front' /frʌnt/ has /fr/ then /nt/. 'People' /ˈpiːpl/.

quests.hint: 'Help yourself to' is one friendly chunk.
quests.explanation: 'Feel free to' and 'help yourself' are the classic hospitality phrases hosts use.
quests.textToSpeak: While you're waiting, feel free to help yourself to some tea or coffee.
quests.correctAnswer: While you're waiting, feel free to help yourself to some tea or coffee.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'While you're' /waɪl jɔː/. 'Yourself' /jɔːˈself/ is stressed on SELF. 'Tea or' links: tee-or.

quests.explanation: The second conditional uses 'had' (past form) to talk about an unreal present situation.
quests.textToSpeak: If I had more time, I'd definitely learn to play the piano.
quests.correctAnswer: If I had more time, I'd definitely learn to play the piano.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Definitely' /ˈdefɪnətli/ is stressed on DEF. 'Piano' /piˈænəʊ/ is stressed on AN. 'Learn' /lɜːn/.

quests.explanation: 'Unless' is a shorter way to say 'if not', and 'quite a while' means a fairly long time.
quests.textToSpeak: Unless you booked in advance, you might have to wait quite a while.
quests.correctAnswer: Unless you booked in advance, you might have to wait quite a while.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Unless' /ənˈles/ is stressed on LESS. 'Advance' /ədˈvɑːns/ ends in /ns/. 'Quite a' links: kwy-tə.

quests.explanation: 'If you happen to' makes a request lighter, as if it's no trouble.
quests.textToSpeak: If you happen to see Sam, could you tell him I called?
quests.correctAnswer: If you happen to see Sam, could you tell him I called?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Happen' /ˈhæpən/ is stressed on HAP. 'Called' /kɔːld/ ends in /ld/. Rise slightly on 'Sam' before the comma.

quests.hint: Chunk the subject: 'the small coffee shop / opposite the post office'.
quests.explanation: A long subject with a place description is typical of spoken recommendations.
quests.textToSpeak: The small coffee shop opposite the post office does the best sandwiches in town.
quests.correctAnswer: The small coffee shop opposite the post office does the best sandwiches in town.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Opposite' /ˈɒpəzɪt/ has three syllables. 'Post office' is stressed on POST. 'Sandwiches' is said in three beats.

quests.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable: say 'some advice', never 'an advice'.
quests.textToSpeak: A friend of mine who works in marketing gave me some great advice.
quests.correctAnswer: A friend of mine who works in marketing gave me some great advice.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Advice' /ədˈvaɪs/ is stressed on VICE. The verb 'advise' ends with /z/ instead. 'Marketing' /ˈmɑːkɪtɪŋ/.

quests.explanation: 'On the third floor' pins down the location, and 'a view of' introduces what you can see.
quests.textToSpeak: The apartment on the third floor has a view of the whole city.
quests.correctAnswer: The apartment on the third floor has a view of the whole city.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Apartment' /əˈpɑːtmənt/ is stressed on PART. 'Third' /θɜːd/. 'Whole' /həʊl/ starts with /h/.

quests.explanation: 'I just wanted to check…' is a soft, polite way to follow up.
quests.textToSpeak: I just wanted to check that you'd got my email from this morning.
quests.correctAnswer: I just wanted to check that you'd got my email from this morning.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Check that' merges the /k/ and /ð/ closely. 'You'd got' /juːd ɡɒt/. 'Morning' /ˈmɔːnɪŋ/.

quests.explanation: 'Do you want me to + verb' offers help, and 'or would you rather' gives an alternative.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you want me to pick you up, or would you rather meet there?
quests.correctAnswer: Do you want me to pick you up, or would you rather meet there?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Would you' becomes 'woodja'. 'Rather' /ˈrɑːðə/ has a voiced /ð/. Rise on 'up', fall on 'there'.

quests.explanation: 'It took us ages to…' is the natural way to say something was slow or hard.
quests.textToSpeak: It took us ages to find a parking space near the stadium.
quests.correctAnswer: It took us ages to find a parking space near the stadium.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Ages' /ˈeɪdʒɪz/. 'Parking' /ˈpɑːkɪŋ/ is stressed on PARK. 'Stadium' /ˈsteɪdiəm/ has three syllables.

quests.explanation: Contrastive stress corrects a misunderstanding by highlighting the exact word that matters.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't say she was late, only that she might be.
quests.correctAnswer: I didn't say she was late, only that she might be.
quests.pronunciationTips: Give 'was' and 'might' extra length and pitch. 'Only that' links: only-that. 'Late' ends with a clean /t/.

quests.explanation: Contrastive stress lets you correct a detail without repeating the whole sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: I asked for the blue folder, not the green one.
quests.correctAnswer: I asked for the blue folder, not the green one.
quests.pronunciationTips: Make 'blue' and 'green' louder and longer. 'Folder' /ˈfəʊldə/ is stressed on FOL. 'Green' /ɡriːn/ has /ɡr/.

quests.explanation: 'It's not that… I'm just…' rejects one explanation and gives the real one.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not that I don't want to go, I'm just really busy.
quests.correctAnswer: It's not that I don't want to go, I'm just really busy.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Want to' can sound like 'wanna'. 'Busy' /ˈbɪzi/ has a short /ɪ/ and a /z/ in the middle. 'Just' ends in /st/.

quests.hint: 'Look over' and 'get back' each work as one unit.
quests.explanation: 'Look over' means check, and 'get back to you' means reply later.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll look over the figures and get back to you by tonight.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll look over the figures and get back to you by tonight.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Get back to' links: ge-tback-tə. 'Tonight' /təˈnaɪt/ is stressed on NIGHT. 'Look over' links.

quests.explanation: 'Take care of' means handle, and 'figure out' means work out.
quests.textToSpeak: We need to figure out who's going to take care of the presentation.
quests.correctAnswer: We need to figure out who's going to take care of the presentation.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Presentation' /ˌprezənˈteɪʃn/ is stressed on TAY. 'Who's' /huːz/ ends in /z/. 'Figure out' links.

quests.explanation: 'Go through' means review step by step, which is very common in meetings.
quests.textToSpeak: Could we go through the main points again before the client arrives?
quests.correctAnswer: Could we go through the main points again before the client arrives?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Through' /θruː/. 'Client' /ˈklaɪənt/ has the diphthong /aɪ/. 'Arrives' /əˈraɪvz/ ends in /vz/.

quests.explanation: 'I'd like to return…' is the standard shop phrase, and 'because' gives a short reason.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to return this sweater because it doesn't fit properly.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to return this sweater because it doesn't fit properly.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Sweater' /ˈswetə/ starts with /sw/. 'Return' /rɪˈtɜːn/. 'Properly' /ˈprɒpəli/ is stressed on PROP.

quests.hint: 'Is there anything' flows as one unit.
quests.explanation: 'Is there anything you can do about…?' is a polite way to raise a complaint.
quests.textToSpeak: Is there anything you can do about the noise from next door?
quests.correctAnswer: Is there anything you can do about the noise from next door?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Noise' /nɔɪz/ ends in /z/. 'Next door' /nekst dɔː/ has a cluster, so keep the /t/ light. 'Anything' /ˈeniθɪŋ/.

quests.hint: 'Charged' begins and ends with affricates: /tʃ/ and /dʒ/.
quests.explanation: The passive 'I've been charged' focuses on what happened to you, and 'so' leads to the request.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been charged twice for the same order, so could you check it?
quests.correctAnswer: I've been charged twice for the same order, so could you check it?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Charged' /tʃɑːdʒd/. 'Twice' /twaɪs/. 'Order' /ˈɔːdə/ is stressed on OR.

quests.explanation: 'The main advantage of + -ing is that…' is a natural frame for giving a reason.
quests.textToSpeak: The main advantage of working from home is that you save time on commuting.
quests.correctAnswer: The main advantage of working from home is that you save time on commuting.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Advantage' /ədˈvɑːntɪdʒ/. 'Commuting' /kəˈmjuːtɪŋ/ is stressed on MYOO. 'Save' /seɪv/ ends in /v/.

quests.hint: 'Notifications' has five syllables, stressed on KAY.
quests.explanation: 'One thing I find difficult is…' is an easy opinion frame, and 'keeping up with' means staying current.
quests.textToSpeak: One thing I find difficult is keeping up with all the notifications.
quests.correctAnswer: One thing I find difficult is keeping up with all the notifications.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Notifications' /ˌnəʊtɪfɪˈkeɪʃnz/. 'Keeping up' links. 'Difficult' /ˈdɪfɪkəlt/ is stressed on DIF.

quests.hint: Slow down on 'exactly why' and finish lightly on 'friendly'.
quests.explanation: 'It's hard to say why' is a common way to admit an impression is a feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: It's hard to say exactly why, but the place just feels friendly.
quests.correctAnswer: It's hard to say exactly why, but the place just feels friendly.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Exactly' /ɪɡˈzæktli/ has a /ɡz/ in the middle. 'Friendly' /ˈfrendli/ ends in /li/. 'Feels' /fiːlz/ ends in /lz/.

quests.explanation: 'I'd love to, but…' is a warm way to refuse, and the reason follows.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd love to come, but I've already made plans for that evening.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd love to come, but I've already made plans for that evening.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Already' /ɔːlˈredi/ is stressed on RED. 'Evening' /ˈiːvnɪŋ/ is often two syllables. 'Made' /meɪd/.

quests.explanation: The preposition 'to' stays at the end of the clause: 'the person you spoke to'.
quests.textToSpeak: The person you spoke to earlier should be able to help you further.
quests.correctAnswer: The person you spoke to earlier should be able to help you further.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Further' /ˈfɜːðə/ has a voiced /ð/. 'Should be able to' has weak forms: shəd-bi-eɪbl-tə. 'Earlier' /ˈɜːliə/.

quests.explanation: 'Right away' means immediately, and the present tense after 'if' points to the future.
quests.textToSpeak: If we can't make it, I'll let you know right away.
quests.correctAnswer: If we can't make it, I'll let you know right away.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Can't' /kɑːnt/ has a strong vowel. 'Right away' /raɪt əˈweɪ/ links. 'I'll' /aɪl/.
